Details: Sudden wars and armed conflicts break out between countries, turning local disputes, opportunistic attacks, and border shocks into a wider chain of fighting.
Liberation shocks create new countries, break old chains of command, and turn subject, republic, or host-survival disputes into broader independence crises.
Diplomatic panic pushes world tension, relation damage, ministries, newspapers, and staff offices into a shared crisis pattern without creating direct war goals or new countries.

Peace incidents reduce conflict through settlements, ceasefires, exhaustion, negotiations, and other de-escalation shocks. White Peace is the low-impact member: it looks for wars that can end without territorial gain.
